title: Bulgaria in brief
description: An overview of Bulgarian history from the Thracians and the medieval empires through five centuries of Ottoman rule to independence and communism. The national history museum sits at the foot of Vitosha mountain.

title: Roman Serdica
episode: Serdica: the Roman city under Sofia
description: A short film on Serdica, the Roman city whose streets and baths were found when the metro was built. Emperor Constantine is said to have called it “my Rome.” The ruins are open to walk through in the station.

title: The Boyana frescoes
description: A short film on Boyana Church, a small medieval church at the edge of the city whose wall paintings from 1259 show people with unusually lifelike faces. Visits last about ten minutes.

title: The Cyrillic alphabet
episode: The Medieval Origins of the Cyrillic Alphabet
place: SS. Cyril and Methodius National Library
description: How the Cyrillic alphabet grew out of the work of Cyril and Methodius, two Byzantine missionaries, and their students in Bulgaria. Statues of the brothers stand in front of the national library.

title: The 1925 cathedral bombing
show: Foreigner BG: Best Info For Expats In Bulgaria
episode: The Biggest Terrorist Act In The History of Bulgaria [Colored footage from 1925]
description: In April 1925, communist militants blew up the roof of Sveta Nedelya Church during a funeral, hoping to kill the king and the government. More than 130 people died. The church was rebuilt in the 1930s.

title: How the Jews were saved
episode: How Bulgarians saved their Jewish neighbors during the Holocaust
description: In March 1943, as trains waited to deport Bulgaria’s Jews, the deputy speaker Dimitar Peshev and other members of parliament protested, along with church leaders. The deportation was called off.

title: The Soviet Army monument
episode: Relief And Anger After Bulgaria Dismantles Massive Soviet Monument
description: A short report from December 2023, when workers took down the figures of the Monument to the Soviet Army, put up in 1954. Locals had repainted its soldiers as superheroes and in the colors of Ukraine.

title: The long revolution
description: A documentary on Bulgaria’s hard road after Todor Zhivkov, its communist leader for 35 years, was pushed out in November 1989. The square in front of the cathedral was the scene of the great rallies of that winter.

title: The Bulgarian voices
episode: Le Mystere des Voix Bulgares - Full Performance (Live on KEXP)
description: The women’s choir, founded at Bulgarian state radio in 1952, singing folk songs in close, ringing harmonies. Its records became a cult hit in the West in the 1980s.

title: The 1994 World Cup
episode: Bulgaria's Golden Generation | USA 1994 | FIFA World Cup
description: Bulgaria had never won a World Cup match before 1994. That summer, Hristo Stoichkov’s team beat Argentina and Germany and reached the semifinal, and Sofia celebrated in the streets.
